anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — the spec covers download, column order, and the empty-collection header, and correctly routes the email to mailer. But it defers the ticket's 10000-widgets-in-60s row with no human answer approving that cut, so not every acme/widgets ticket row is delivered.
findings:
- [blocker] scope @ "An export of 10000 widgets completes within 60s. - deferred: acme/widgets#78" and Goal "The 60s performance row is deferred" — the `deferred:` disposition has no matching cut question or user answer in `Human input`. The verbatim block only says "Implement the widgets CSV export described in this ticket. Mailer owns the notification.", which approves no deferral of the performance row. → Mark the row `in-scope`, drop the deferral sentence from Goal, and make the benchmark a required verification step. Alternatively, get and quote an explicit user answer that picks this cut. — probed: Human input block (inlined) - no cut question or answer for the 60s row
- [major] gap @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000." — the problem says users download "their widgets", but the design never says how the query is limited to the requesting user's or account's widgets. It also does not say what happens for unauthenticated or unauthorized requests to GET /widgets/export.csv. As written, an implementer could export every widget. → Add: "Scope the query to widgets owned by the authenticated user (same authorization as the collection page); unauthenticated requests get the same response as the collection page (redirect/401)". Add a request test showing another user's widgets are excluded. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope." — the step is conditional, so verification of the performance AC is optional. Once the row is in scope, this must be a required, pass/fail check. → Reword to: "Run the 10000-widget benchmark; fail if request start to complete response exceeds 60s." Name where it runs (CI job or documented local command). — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Encode id, name, and status with standard CSV quoting" — the spec names no standard, line terminator, or BOM policy, and does not say how `status` is serialized (enum name, label, or integer). → Specify RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF or LF, no BOM (or BOM), and the exact `status` representation, e.g. the stored enum string. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut
